I think, unfortunately, that this video gets a number of things wrong. Firstly, an increase in the number of people performing a job is not evidence of a lack of impact from automation, i.e. there would likely be a greater demand for more or more skilled pilots today in the absence of autopilot. Secondly, the use of job titles as a proxy for jobs is misleading because jobs may have the same title in different decades, but may have vastly different required skills, career opportunities, and day-to-day tasks. For example, bank tellers or customer service. Finally, though this point is much more arguable, the main point of this new wave of automation being scarier than previous ones is the number of individuals who went into debt to procure the skills that are about to be automated away. The size of this group is debatable, but it ranges anywhere from all thought workers(tech bro take) to just some fields(conservatively). The extent of automation will also range. These people, who took on debt expecting that their gained knowledge or skills will allow them to earn at a premium(in order to pay back what they owe!) may just be flat out of luck. Depending on who you believe on this, this may be a small or potentially a significant fraction of the population. They will probably still have a job, albeit not at their expected premium, so I hope you see my point that ai “taking” the job is a misleading way to represent ai automation fears. I enjoyed the video, and I think that we should all be thinking about this topic, but trying to justify what we all want to hear with statistics and stories that don’t accurately fit the situation does people who as a result may end up unprepared a disservice. I really like this channel because of the interesting topics it chooses to cover, and I would to see a bit more seriousness and thought behind the statistics and stories that get represented here. Treat us like a community who can bear the truth in these important topics, and the millions of us who listen will be able to see the world more clearly and make it a better place as a result. Thanks!

How do you think we get Middle or High level software engineers? Through experience. When Low level software engineers earn enough experience, they become Middle and then High level. And whos job AI is taking away? It will be no problem if AI will take job from High level software engineers. But it's not what happening right now. AI is taking the job from Low level software engineers. Because it's simply not good enough. It's becoming the base of the companies. and the demand for Middle and then High level is rising. But they will eventually run out of it. And everything will collapse. It's like you was feeding corn to the cows to make beef. And then you say, "Well, I need beef so why should I grow corn. These kinds of horrible practices by companies, staffing and corporate, are why I stopped being a recruiter. They pull the wool over our eyes too, listing their requirements for hiring a potential candidate, but when we want feedback as to why they haven't hired any the dozens of candidates submitted, we get yelled at, or even fired for just wanting to know how to provide them better potential employees. Like any profession, some recruiters are absolutely deplorable, some do try to help others, but I was often thanked for my transparency by those potential candidates. I used to provide them resources like Delilah Bell and other websites/social media pages which post jobs; a few wrote back to me after some weeks saying they were able to find a job from one of those resources. But it's beyond heartbreaking that so many capable people are being played with by corporate America.
